items.summary: NANOROBOT-ENHANCED DIGITAL TWINS OF BRAIN STATE AT THE LIMIT A multiscale, uncertainty-aware research atlas on microrobotic observations, neural inverse problems, active model discrimination and the limits of computational brain twins. This research monograph asks whether additional microscale observations or strictly bounded reversible experiments can distinguish competing neural-state models that explain conventional measurements equally well. The twin is explicitly defined as a versioned scientific belief, not a digital person, a mind reader or a clinically validated instrument. Its objective is not maximum model complexity but improved identifiability, calibrated prediction under new conditions and faithful retention of failed hypotheses. The work develops five layers: multiscale neural and microenvironment state representation; posterior equivalence and prior sensitivity; non-clinical safe experimental design; frozen-version forking, rollback and reference ancestry; and blind prospective validation against classical state-space systems and independently specified alternatives. Its research architecture includes 30 distinct mathematical derivation plates linked to later chapters, 82 chapters with five independently paginated research sections apiece, 200 detailed Research Gates and 33 revisable Phoenix Answer Embryos. A DOI evidence ledger identifies existing support for brain modeling, latent neural dynamics, experiment design and preclinical microrobot tracking while preventing those sources from being mistaken for evidence of the proposed integrated system. Key research questions include: Can two equally accurate virtual brains be separated by a small, permissible observation? How can the effect of a measurement itself be separated from neural change? When does a prior dominate the inferred brain state? Can the model predict unseen function rather than reconstruct a training signal? Can another laboratory reproduce a rejected twin and safely return to an earlier version? SCIENTIFIC STATUS AND LIMITATIONS This is a forward-looking, non-clinical research synthesis and experimental hypothesis architecture. It provides no personal medical advice, patient-specific interpretations or instruction to deliver neural interventions. Existing murine microrobot tracking and virtual-brain modeling studies do not establish autonomous neural nanorobot readout, human safety, privacy-sensitive mind inference or therapeutic efficacy. Proposed formulas, experiments, research gates and answer embryos are not newly validated biological laws or executed experiments. The work keeps independent safety vetoes, privacy, external reproducibility and explicit model retirement as first-class constraints. Research questions remain open to refutation, correction and reconstruction by future human and AI researchers.

items.summary: Fisher information metric tensors for the 41 held-out SONICOM test subjects, as used in “Evaluating Spatial Discriminability Preservation in HRTF Upsampling Using Fisher Information” (D. Bassett). Code and reproduction instructions: https://github.com/domfrbassett/fisher-rao-hrtf-upsampling What the tensors are At each of the 793 directions of the SONICOM grid, the 2×2 tensor g = JᵀΣ⁻¹J describes how well the auditory cues separate that direction from its neighbours. J is the spatial Jacobian of the cues: Barumerli monaural PGE features, ILD and MaxIACCe-transformed ITD, each fitted with real spherical harmonics. Σ holds the cue noise (σ_mon = 1.25 dB, σ_ILD = 1 dB, σ_ITD = 0.569). All fields are low-pass filtered at 16 kHz before the cues are extracted. The tensor is expressed in a local tangent basis u₁ = a × r, u₂ = r × u₁, where a = z, or y when |r_z| > 0.9, and its units are d′² per rad². Contents metric_tensors.zip has one folder per subject, metric_tensors/subject_####/ , containing 25 files per subject (1,025 in total): reference_metric_tensor.mat : the dense measured HRTF. <METHOD>_N###_metric_tensor.mat : one file per reconstruction. There are six methods: SUpDEq_SH , SUpDEq_MCA , SUpDEq_NN_MCA_6dB (SUpDEq-Natural-MCA in the paper), SUpDEq_Bary_MCA_6dB , RANF and FSP_AE . Each is reconstructed from N = 100, 19, 5 and 3 retained directions. The 164 natural-neighbour and barycentric files at N = 5 and 3 have status “ not_applicable ”. The interpolation is undefined for those masks, so these files carry no tensors. Variables in each file: metricTensor : the tensors at SH order 6 [2×2×793]. familyGram : per-cue-family Gram matrices JᵀJ before noise weighting, at SH orders 4, 6 and 8 [2×2×793×3 families×3 orders]. They let you recompute the tensors with other noise values or SH orders. In reconstruction files only: crossFamilyGram : the unsymmetrised cross terms J_refᵀ J_recon, same layout as familyGram . airmByDirection : the pointwise AIRM discrepancy from the reference. Metadata: coordinates (Cartesian and azimuth/elevation in degrees), cue band, noise values (reference files only), status (“ completed ” or “ not_applicable ”) and, for not-applicable files, a message giving the reason. SHA256SUMS.txt lists a checksum for every file. Format and use The files are MATLAB v7.3 (HDF5), so MATLAB, h5py or any HDF5 reader can open them. Note that h5py reverses MATLAB’s axis order. scripts/fisher_lib.py in the repository reads them and recomputes tensors, AIRM and thresholds from the Gram matrices. To rerun the analysis scripts, unzip into results/evaluation/ so the subject folders sit in results/evaluation/metric_tensors/ . Provenance Produced with run_evaluation("tensors") from the repository above. The values are numerically identical to the tensor files behind results/evaluation/full_evaluation_summary.csv ; this run additionally stores the cross terms. The tensors are derived from the SONICOM HRTF Dataset (Engel et al., J. Audio Eng. Soc. 71(5), 2023, doi:10.17743/jaes.2022.0066). The SONICOM HRTFs are released under the MIT licence. This work develops research begun for the author’s B.Sc. dissertation at Birmingham City University.

items.summary: This technical note documents a conditional mathematical correspondence between the static spatial kernel used in conventional electromagnetic potential theory and the fixed-source gravitational potential in Lisa Doumbouya’s Harmonic Physics programme. Under supplied three-dimensional Euclidean geometry, spherical symmetry and stated boundary conditions, the derivation gives the static Green function 1/(4πr). Applying the existing gravitational source normalization yields the potential −μ/r, whose radial derivative gives the inward acceleration −μ/r². The note distinguishes potential, field amplitude, intensity, acceleration and optical measurement conversion, keeping geometric normalization separate from the distance exponent. The optical phase-ruler results are reviewed alongside the GRACE-FO forward forecasts. Calibrated reconstruction using measured phase retained micrometre-scale agreement with processed microwave ranging, while some forward models produced much larger errors. These results do not establish exponential error growth or identify a unique physical cause. The correspondence uses established mathematics and remains conditional on the supplied geometry, source calibration and physical interpretation. It does not establish an electromagnetic mechanism of gravity or derive spatial geometry from foundational Phase. The note includes the analytical proof, assumptions, evidence boundaries and requirements for a subsequent physical test. No new experimental data are introduced.

Numerical signal alignment alone cannot establish continuity of intention. Two systems may encode different signals while supporting the same functional command, or produce nearly identical latent representations while mapping to incompatible actions. The volume formulates meaning continuity as a conditional, falsifiable engineering and scientific hypothesis. It connects device-specific observation models, neural recording instability, task and action ontologies, paired old/new sensing periods, latent manifold bridging, longitudinal recalibration, calibrated abstention, functional validation, and an accessible right to reject the proposed migration. Its central commitment is that no amount of predictive accuracy can compensate for invalid authorization, an unverified physical reference, or loss of independent control. The research atlas comprises thirty connected mathematical derivations, eighty-two research chapters, and 410 independently paginated chapter sections that examine observables, inverse explanations, discriminating experiments, uncertainty and noncompensable safeguards, and independent requalification. Two hundred detailed Research Gates propose future falsification and handoff programs, while thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos preserve revisable candidate approaches rather than immutable conclusions. A claim-scoped DOI evidence ledger connects the study to published work on neural recording drift, decoder adaptation, manifold alignment, longitudinal neural interfaces, speech BCIs, user preferences, and neurotechnology ethics. The book is designed for both human researchers and future AI research systems. Its formulas, chapter cross-links, DOI anchors, competing models, negative-result requirements, and successor-focused research cards provide structured entry points for independent reconstruction and informed disagreement. The visual presentation combines ivory pages, navy and teal typography, and large gold mathematical plates, while mathematical expressions are also recorded in searchable source notation and a separate Excel reference index. This is a prospective, nonclinical research architecture. It does not report new patient experiments, demonstrate safe autonomous human neurovascular microrobots, establish a universal device-migration system, or claim continuity of private thoughts, consciousness, or personal identity. Scientific benefit remains conditional on explicit task definitions, qualified device evidence, legitimate permissions, external validation, and the successor's freedom to reject a failed bridge. Research question: What should remain invariant when an interface changes, and who has the authority to say that its meaning has changed?

items.summary: SELF-CALIBRATING NANO-NEURAL INTERFACES AND REFERENCE LINEAGE AT THE LIMIT Built-In References × Drift Attribution × Independent Functional Requalification STARLI / Institute XXIII / Research Flagship 17 PUBLICATION DESCRIPTION When a long-running neural interface changes, is the cause the sensor, the surrounding tissue, or the decoder? An adaptive algorithm can restore predictive accuracy while obscuring the physical origin of its own correction. This book proposes a rigorous, falsifiable architecture for self-calibrating nano-neural interfaces that must retain the scientific history of every reference and every update. Its central axiom is that self-calibration does not imply self-certification: measurement claims, permission to change, electrode safety and functional benefit demand independent evidence. The first coupling is the existence of physically traceable internal references that can be challenged against electrically and temporally independent standards. The second is a source-aware drift-diagnostic process that distinguishes electronics gain, electrode-tissue transfer, tissue-like surrogate changes, changing source signals and model/feature drift, explicitly recording instances of nonidentifiability. The third is external functional requalification, which can reject an apparently successful update after hidden-domain testing, material or reference replacement, loss of selectivity, missing raw observations, or inability to reproduce the frozen predecessor. This research monograph is divided into seven causal layers and 82 chapters. Five major subsections of each chapter are assigned independent pages, yielding 410 separately paginated technical essays. Thirty gold mathematical derivations are linked from chapter-opening equations to discriminating experiments. The mathematics includes augmented state-space observability, nonlinear observation functions, source-separation Jacobians, Kalman innovations, impedance spectroscopy, covariance propagation, change-point statistics, conformal coverage, selective risk, hard-veto constrained update eligibility, reference-bridge covariance, exact rollback and cross-laboratory requalification. A displayed formula is a candidate analytical instrument with stated dimensions and assumptions, not a discovered biological law. Two hundred detailed Research Gates are preserved at the rear: 82 interrogate source identifiability, another 82 challenge independent physical and evidential hard vetoes, and 36 require third-party reconstruction of a frozen reference history. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose revisable architectures, beginning with the Neural Interface Calibration Passport. The Passport ties an interface's physical identity to the raw analog and digitized record, calibrated unit chain, hardware reference ancestors, model and feature checksums, reasons for changing any reference, failed updates, revoked permissions, blinded requalification and rollback. These are proposed evidence structures, not commercially validated devices. The DOI bibliography contains 18 unique external research records covering chronic intracortical signal instability, low-dimensional BCI stabilization, decoder adaptation, long-term electrode-tissue behavior, complex impedance metrology, electrochemical reference limits, neural interface materials and conformal uncertainty under covariate shift. Selected publisher and PubMed pages were consulted for source metadata. Their findings cannot establish efficacy of the new self-calibration architecture; source-specific claims and independent replication would be necessary.

items.summary: This working paper develops a relational Phase interpretation of black holes within the Harmonic Physics research programme, using general relativity, exact Kerr geometry and semiclassical black-hole thermodynamics as its physical baseline. It examines how phase organisation, temporal reference, observer accessibility and information persistence might relate to black-hole closure. Within the proposed framework, a phase-cycle is a closed relational structure that supports recurrence. Measured succession requires distinguishable relations and persistent records, while geometry and causal history are treated as observer-level reconstructions. The temporal-anchor hypothesis concerns a deeper terminal condition at which the parent domain loses the internally usable references needed to resolve further clocks and geometry. This proposed condition is kept distinct from the regular event horizon, across which local evolution continues. Observation is described through a joint observation relation among admitted source organisation, a physical channel and an observer-capable organisation. Source state, coupling and registered record retain separate roles; changes in accessibility may alter registration while the source organisation persists. The paper consolidates three bounded mathematical findings: exact Kerr ingoing and outgoing endpoints can have opposite trapped and anti-trapped orientations with the same mass and spin parameters; spherical source/exterior matching leaves the transition law undetermined; and a leading slow-rotation calculation permits the same sign of angular momentum in closing and opening configurations. These results establish compatibility within the stated geometric constructions. A physical transition mechanism remains to be derived. Black-to-white-hole models provide external theoretical comparisons. Return to the original exterior and the opening of a daughter phase are treated as distinct hypotheses, each requiring an appropriate causal structure, state map and conservation accounting. The remaining requirements include an invariant parent-relative terminal criterion, a physical Phase-to-boundary map, transition dynamics, information and entropy accounting, and a stable nonperturbative rotating completion. The paper remains a developing theoretical interpretation supported by standard-geometry comparisons and bounded symbolic checks. It does not establish a physical black-to-white transition, information recovery through evaporation or a daughter universe. Version 2.3, dated 17 October 2026, updates observation and self-nesting terminology, clarifies geodesic incompleteness and fixed-angular-momentum assumptions, and refreshes the references. The existing displayed equations and reported test results are retained. keywords: Phase Theory; black holes; event horizons; geodesic incompleteness; relational time; phase contraction; information accessibility; singularity; white holes; quantum gravity.

items.summary: mm-ADL-Home is a cross-environment millimeter-wave radar point-cloud dataset for human activity recognition in furnished residential environments. The dataset was collected in four indoor environments comprising three simulated bachelor-unit layouts and one real bachelor unit, using the same activity taxonomy and radar configuration as the mm-ADL dataset (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22405011).  Each participant–environment recording is preserved as a continuous point-cloud stream and includes: (1) point_cloud.csv , containing radar point-cloud observations; (2) frame_labels.csv , containing frame-level activity annotations; (3) timestamps.csv , providing the temporal correspondence between radar and annotation frames; and (4) location_annotations.csv , containing the intervals used to register the radar sensor and landmark furniture in the radar coordinate system. The activity taxonomy covers locomotion, sitting and lying transitions, stationary sitting and lying, simulated falls, and floor-to-standing recovery. Location annotations identify sittable furniture, lieable furniture, kitchen locations, entry locations, and the radar sensor origin. These annotations support the reconstruction of room-level spatial context and furniture landmarks on the horizontal radar coordinate plane. The dataset contains complete recordings without a prescribed windowing or segmentation scheme, allowing users to implement their own preprocessing, temporal segmentation, domain adaptation, and evaluation protocols. Synchronized RGB recordings used during annotation are not included in the public release. Participant identifiers are pseudonymous.

items.summary: Data and analytical software for thermally activated Fe-SMA fibre-reinforced concrete This repository accompanies the article “Analytical modelling of thermally activated iron-based shape memory alloy fibre concrete: Finite transfer and capacity compatibility”. It provides the numerical source data, analytical implementation, calibration inputs, and results used to prepare the final article. The work examines finite fibre–matrix transfer, thermally activated composite response, cohesive-law identification, and the compatibility of reported strengths with uncertain fibre orientation and tensile capacity. The deposit contains one final analysis snapshot. It includes the reference formulation and the baselines, thermal alternatives, and cohesive-law candidates examined in the article. These are parts of the reported scientific assessment, rather than separate manuscript versions. Superseded model results, development archives, manuscript drafts, and unrelated source files are excluded. Contents • data/ contains numerical representations of published response curves, reported group statistics, study metadata, fixed constituent and pullout calibrations, optimizer initialization values, and published experimental/finite-element comparison curves. Curve identifiers preserve the link to the source study and figure. These are processed publication-based data, rather than original instrument records. • model/ contains the executable analysis scripts. items.summary: Decentralized multi-robot shape formation in GPS-denied environments is important for search-and-rescue and disaster response. Conventional consensus-based formation controllers can violate safe separation, oscillate, or stall when communication degrades, sensors are noisy, or an agent drops out. This paper proposes a resilient decentralized controller that combines Huber-weighted consensus and Exponential Moving Average (EMA) state estimation with a Dual-Layer Artificial Potential Field (APF) safety barrier. The first layer adds an anti-symmetric lateral deflection to resolve head-on encounters between peers; the second applies a normal-plus-tangential circulation field around static obstacles. The framework is evaluated on five simulated nonholonomic differential-drive robots in Gazebo Harmonic (ROS 2 Jazzy). Three runs are compared: a linear consensus baseline, the same baseline under faults (15% packet loss, 50-150 ms delay, σ = 0.18 m sensor noise, and a mid-run agent blackout), and the proposed controller under the same faults. The fault-free baseline reached the pentagon fastest (0.0156 m final RMS error) but its minimum separation fell to 0.3918 m, with 31 logged violations of the 0.50 m margin. Under faults the baseline reached 0.0546 m with 5 violations (minimum 0.4833 m). The proposed controller recorded no violations, kept a minimum separation of 0.6757 m, and reached 0.0368 m final error, at the cost of slower convergence (about 21 s versus about 12-15 s). Results are from single simulation runs, and the safety barrier is empirical rather than formally guaranteed.

items.summary: Emergency-stop circuits built by engineering technology students are routinely treated as safe once they pass a functional test at commissioning, yet the relay contact welding that dominates their failure modes is invisible to such tests and accumulates silently across the workshop's operating life. The framework represents a student-built circuit as a series safety function whose integrity is degraded by contact welding, and derives the conditions under which a welded contact converts a demanded stop into an undetected loss of safety function. A replication-based evaluation of the before-after-control-impact estimator was conducted under a declared variance structure with a between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0, a residual standard deviation of 4.5 and an intraclass correlation of 0.64, across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The evaluation indicates that 54 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power, and that the minimum detectable effect at 80% power falls as the number of clusters rises. The framework proposes that workshop safety assurance should shift from commissioning-time functional testing to integrity monitoring that is sensitive to contact welding, and the design analysis implies that cluster-level evaluations of such interventions require cluster counts well above those typical of single-institution studies.

items.summary: The Voynich Manuscript exhibits strong statistical regularities, but the distinction between recoverable grammar and recoverable lexical meaning remains unresolved. This study asks how far a progressively frozen, cross-validated analysis can reconstruct the manuscript’s internal word-building system without assigning meanings from illustrations, candidate languages, or post-hoc English paraphrase. Using canonical transcription, protected holdout partitions, alternate-transcription replication, exact host substitutions, and adversarial stopping rules, the analysis recovers a cumulative left-edge morphology, a transferable inventory of 39 surface CORE-0 stem/bodies, reproducible host-by-right-state coupling, a stable K/T referential contrast, and a directed network among powered lexical cores. The 39-core inventory predicts protected-frame combinatorics and content-blind contextual fingerprints out of sample, while attempts to decompose these bodies into a deeper transferable root layer fail. Nine recurring hosts show strongly replicated coupling to EY/EEY/EDY right-edge states, supporting a distributed morphological paradigm rather than independent left- and right-side systems. A 28-node directed CORE network also replicates across canonical calibration, untouched Holdout, and alternate-transcription tests, yielding neutral outbound- and inbound-biased stem classes without requiring part-of-speech or semantic assignments. On the project’s fully constrained 1,609-line benchmark, 12,299 of 12,495 positions are role-naturalizable (98.4314%), leaving 196 opaque positions. This percentage is explicitly a conditional benchmark-maturity statistic, not a measure of literal plaintext recovery or manuscript-wide translation accuracy. Repeated attempts to cross from structural organization to ordinary lexical meaning—including deeper-root induction, topic clustering, functional-neighborhood anchoring, local lexical syntax, illustration matching, source-language fitting, and prospective semantic transfer—fail the project’s promotion criteria. The resulting contribution is therefore a structural decipherment rather than a lexical one: a reproducible grammatical and morphological architecture together with an empirically identified lexical-identifiability ceiling. The work extends, but is distinct from, the earlier controlled-translation release at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22049207.
items.title: Structural Decipherment Without Lexical Recovery: A Cross-Validated Morphological Analysis of the Voynich Manuscript

items.summary: Oscilloscope probe compensation kits circulate between teaching laboratories, yet the calibration status of a kit is rarely transferred with the same rigour as the instrument it serves. the present analysis treats cross-course calibration transfer as a metrological problem and evaluates, by round-robin design, how bandwidth attenuation in a probe kit propagates into measurement discrepancy bounds when the kit is moved between courses. The evaluation is a replication-based characterisation of the before-after-control-impact estimator under a declared variance structure (between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5, intraclass correlation = 0.64), with power estimated across 2000 design cells at cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points.54 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power, and that the minimum detectable effect falls steeply as cluster count rises from 8 to 32. A first-order attenuation model links probe bandwidth to the fractional amplitude error at the test frequency, and the round-robin design is shown to bound the transfer discrepancy that a receiving course can expect. The contribution is a design-level calibration-transfer protocol that makes the discrepancy bound explicit before a kit leaves its home course, rather than after a student records a suspect waveform.

items.summary: Emergency-stop circuits built by engineering technology students are routinely treated as safe once they pass a functional test at commissioning, yet the relay contact welding that dominates their failure modes is invisible to such tests and accumulates silently across the workshop's operating life. The framework represents a student-built circuit as a series safety function whose integrity is degraded by contact welding, and derives the conditions under which a welded contact converts a demanded stop into an undetected loss of safety function. A replication-based evaluation of the before-after-control-impact estimator was conducted under a declared variance structure with a between-cluster standard deviation of 6.0, a residual standard deviation of 4.5 and an intraclass correlation of 0.64, across 2000 replications per design cell for cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points. The evaluation indicates that 54 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power, and that the minimum detectable effect at 80% power falls as the number of clusters rises. The framework proposes that workshop safety assurance should shift from commissioning-time functional testing to integrity monitoring that is sensitive to contact welding, and the design analysis implies that cluster-level evaluations of such interventions require cluster counts well above those typical of single-institution studies.

items.summary: Space Semiconductor Fabrication and Starship Nanofoundries at the Limit English Description and Research Position This research monograph asks which semiconductor unit processes could achieve a defensible mission advantage in microgravity, vacuum, radiation, remote-operation, and closed-resource environments. It does not assume that a complete advanced fab can operate in space. Instead, it compares crystal growth, deposition, etching, lithography, metrology, bonding, packaging, repair, and recycling against ground manufacture plus transport, launched spares, on-orbit packaging, and local repair. Every claimed advantage must survive matched controls, full functional qualification, and explicit mass, energy, heat, crew, contamination, maintenance, waste, and return ledgers. The volume contains 82 chapters with five research sections per chapter, 30 linked formula derivations, 200 detailed Research Gates, DOI-anchored references, and a formula-chapter-experiment-Gate crosswalk. Its central contribution is a mission-scale evidence architecture that connects process physics to contained workcells, independent metrology, safe autonomy, repair, return, circular resources, cross-platform reproduction, and successor reconstruction. Safety and irreversible environmental harm operate as hard vetoes rather than compensable score components. The literature base includes peer-reviewed DOI sources on microgravity semiconductor growth, in-space manufacturing, additive nanomanufacturing, atomic-layer processing, radiation effects, lunar resource extraction, digital twins, autonomous laboratories, and reproducible science. Recent orbital results are treated as early evidence for specific mechanisms, not as confirmation of a complete space foundry. Core research question Under what physical and mission conditions can a semiconductor unit process performed in space outperform ground manufacture plus transport or a narrower in-space alternative while preserving safety, resource closure, qualification, and independent reconstruction? Research architecture • Space-specific process advantage and strongest comparator • Environmental physics and bounded process window • Closed mass energy heat contamination and evidence ledgers • Autonomy safeing repair return and independent qualification • Cross-platform reproduction successor rebuild and retirement Recommended citation note This is an exploratory research architecture. Candidate equations are measurement and mission-decision instruments, not universal laws. Empirical use requires process-specific units, preregistration, matched controls, aerospace and semiconductor expertise, independent qualification, and cross-platform replication.

items.summary: Image harmonization methods adjust the colour and lighting of an object pasted into a photograph so that it looks native to its new scene, and they are ranked by average error on one benchmark whose test images are real photographs with one object recoloured. One photograph can yield several such test images, and the benchmark promises that no photograph appears in both the training and the test split. We find that 1,399 photographs do, and the composites built on them are a quarter of the test set. Duplicate checks over file names or bytes miss this, because every composite is a different file. On that quarter the three methods we score end to end read two to five times lower error than on the rest, but most of the gap is composition rather than the sharing: the shared composites come almost entirely from one of the benchmark's four source collections, and inside that collection the gap falls to about one and a half times. An official score is therefore an average over two populations, mixed in a proportion the benchmark does not report. We release a test list of 5,581 composites whose construction identities do not appear in training, with four near-duplicate pairs disclosed rather than removed, adoptable without retraining at the price of one rescore per checkpoint. We leave open whether the sharing itself changes what a model learns. Contents of this record. The paper, the supplement, the LaTeX source of both, the record metadata and the licence statement. The identity matcher, the composite-locality and sensitivity checks, the CPU tests, the official iHarmony4 lists and the corrected test list are released under the MIT license at https://github.com/Buljic/only-means-only . What this record does not contain. No dataset, no images, no masks, no model checkpoints and no third-party baseline code or weights; those are described and cited by the paper and remain under their own terms. This is a preprint. It has not been peer reviewed. Licensed CC BY 4.0.

items.summary: This report establishes an exact conditional mathematical correspondence between a specified two-component phase model and the sine-Gordon equation appearing in a classical string-theory reduction. Developed within the Harmonic Physics Research Programme, the model uses interacting phase components labelled expansion and contraction in the proposed physical interpretation. For a continuum action with a cosine interaction, constant coefficients and equal component propagation speeds, an invertible change of variables separates the dynamics into an exact nonlinear sine-Gordon equation for the normalized relative phase and a free wave equation for the common phase. The interaction potential can also be expressed through the squared magnitude of the difference between two complex phase components. The derivation retains the full nonlinearity, extending the correspondence beyond the small-angle approximation. Direct numerical evolution of the original component fields provides a reproducible check at finite relative-phase amplitude. The reported breather benchmark reaches a peak relative-phase excursion of approximately 2.574 radians, with a maximum sampled error of approximately 6.3 × 10⁻⁹ radians over two oscillation periods. Component amplitudes remain fixed. Interaction-removal and unequal-speed controls document the failure to recover the same target when the specified conditions are changed. The string-theory connection is examined through the Pohlmeyer reduction of classical strings on R_t × S². A separate conventional kink embedding is checked against the local geometric constraints and string equations of motion. The evolved phase breather is not reconstructed as a string. The established result is a conditional correspondence between reduced classical equations; a full physical or quantum equivalence between the proposed phase model and string theory remains unestablished. Version 1.0 includes the standalone report and an accompanying reproducibility archive containing mathematical derivations, executable Python scripts, numerical settings, sampled synthetic data, control results, figures, source provenance, checksum manifests and reproduction instructions. A documented replay of the retained calculation and an AI-assisted computational audit support inspection and reuse of the reported results. items.summary: This archive is provided as artifact material for the article "Synthesis and Verification of Register Automata over Data Sequences" for SETTA 2026. Abstract: Data sequences, such as time series, traces, and sensor streams, are words over large or infinite data domains. Their properties often depend on comparisons between values at different positions, which finite automata cannot express directly. We study synthesis and verification for Deterministic Register Automata (DRAs) over ordered data sequences. DRAs combine finite control with registers for remembered data values, providing compact symbolic descriptions of quantitative sequence languages. Our technical core is a local-search synthesis procedure and an exact robustness checker for DRAs. We fix the alphabet theory to ordered rationals $(\Q;<,=)$ with rational guard constants and use non-negative affine accumulator costs. For a fixed number of DRA registers, the checker runs in polynomial time; its dependence on that number is exponential. It reduces robustness to coverability and then to a shortest-path problem. Since the search ranges over $\Q^+$, it produces variable-length witnesses and, for RAA-definable alignment costs such as DTW, explores a counterexample space with no a priori length bound. As an application, we use learned DRAs as interpretable surrogates for queried neural sequence classifiers. A probably approximately correct (PAC) validation loop refines rejected candidates, returns genuine non-robustness witnesses for the classifier when found, and accepts a surrogate only with statistical guarantees for fidelity and local stability. We implement the framework in \textit{RAExc}, enabling the synthesis of interpretable automata and the verification of their robustness. We evaluate the approach on benchmark languages and sequentialized MNIST, demonstrating high accuracy while verifying the robustness of the learned automata.
items.title: Synthesis and Verification of Transformer Programs

items.summary: Decentralized multi-robot shape formation in GPS-denied environments is important for search-and-rescue and disaster response. Conventional consensus-based formation controllers can violate safe separation, oscillate, or stall when communication degrades, sensors are noisy, or an agent drops out. This paper proposes a resilient decentralized controller that combines Huber-weighted consensus and Exponential Moving Average (EMA) state estimation with a Dual-Layer Artificial Potential Field (APF) safety barrier. The first layer adds an anti-symmetric lateral deflection to resolve head-on encounters between peers; the second applies a normal-plus-tangential circulation field around static obstacles. The framework is evaluated on five simulated nonholonomic differential-drive robots in Gazebo Harmonic (ROS 2 Jazzy). Three runs are compared: a linear consensus baseline, the same baseline under faults (15% packet loss, 50-150 ms delay, σ = 0.18 m sensor noise, and a mid-run agent blackout), and the proposed controller under the same faults. The fault-free baseline reached the pentagon fastest (0.0156 m final RMS error) but its minimum separation fell to 0.3918 m, with 31 logged violations of the 0.50 m margin. Under faults the baseline reached 0.0546 m with 5 violations (minimum 0.4833 m). The proposed controller recorded no violations, kept a minimum separation of 0.6757 m, and reached 0.0368 m final error, at the cost of slower convergence (about 21 s versus about 12-15 s). Results are from single simulation runs, and the safety barrier is empirical rather than formally guaranteed.
items.title: Resilient Decentralized Shape Formation of Multi-Robot Swarms Under Adversarial Real-World Faults in High-Complexity Disaster Environments

items.summary: Large language models often penalize multilingual users through hidden 'tokenizer taxes' caused by subword fragmentation. Geographic proper nouns offer a controlled stress case for this distributional asymmetry, as they are standardized, cross-linguistically available entities whose orthographic forms frequently mismatch tokenizer training distributions. We introduce the Cross-Linguistic Orthographic Uniqueness Score (CLOUS), a character-level metric based on Shannon surprisal that quantifies the orthographic rarity of localized country names. We evaluate CLOUS on a controlled corpus of 249 ISO-registered country names; generalization to other geographic entity types remains future work. We evaluate CLOUS against tokenization fertility for six production tokenizers spanning three algorithm families across eleven languages and seven script families. Using Spearman rank correlation with Benjamini-Hochberg correction, CLOUS shows significant associative strength with fertility in 61 of 65 valid language-tokenizer combinations. As a screening tool for high-fragmentation entities, CLOUS achieves ROC-AUC = 0.850 and F1 = 0.740, correctly identifying approximately three-quarters of the highest-fragmentation entities from orthographic properties alone. We further show that CLOUS correlates with fertility more strongly than length-based baselines across all evaluated scripts, and outperforms a character bigram surprisal model in 69.2% of tested combinations, particularly for logographic, syllabic, and Latin scripts. Conversely, the bigram baseline proves superior for morphophonologically complex scripts like Arabic and Devanagari, indicating that tokenizer fragmentation is driven by local orthographic context in some scripts and absolute character rarity in others. Script family appears to be the primary driver of CLOUS-fertility correlation strength, with effect sizes ranging from modest for Latin-script languages ) to large for non-Latin scripts (   up to 0.686 for Japanese). These findings suggest that CLOUS may be useful as a lightweight pre-tokenization diagnostic for multilingual NLP pipelines.
items.title: Estimating Cross-Lingual Tokenization Fragmentation Risk: A Frequency-Based Uniqueness Score for Geographic Entities

items.summary: Version 2.0 is a substantive revision of version 1.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19174862). It supersedes the earlier procedural interpretation and its exclusion of competing explanations. The revised title is Structural Organization and Interpretive Limits of the Phaistos Disc. Reproduced descriptive findings are retained; failed model comparisons and photographic uncertainties are reported explicitly. The earlier version remains available through the record version history. We examine whether reproducible structural observations on the Phaistos Disc support a procedural interpretation. A pinned numerical transcription contains 242 main-sign positions, including one unreadable position, 45 readable sign types, 61 divider-defined groups and 18 supplementary stroke annotations. Source review reconciles counting and numbering conventions while retaining unresolved photographic uncertainty. The 02-to-12 side contrast persists after exact-family collapse. Adding side to a fixed position-only pairing predictor improves held-family loss by 0.082738 nats, but its exact conditional tail of 0.075 fails the frozen support rule. A positional mixture fails to outperform a bigram baseline. A separate directional test of the proposed 07-to-27 recovery relationship fails, with a one-sided permutation tail of 0.884. Supplementary-stroke comparisons have insufficient controlled overlap for the specified exact test. The work documents organization and constrains specific interpretations without establishing procedural functions or phonetic values. Corpus, code, protocols, full results and uncertainty ledgers accompany the paper.

items.summary: Research compendium for the article "Climate warming is projected to reduce and redistribute Aedes albopictus abundance, away from Po Valley hotspots towards Alpine margins" (M. C. Darılmaz, Science of the Total Environment; manuscript STOTEN-D-26-01129R1). The study predicts weekly ovitrap egg counts of the Asian tiger mosquito at 149 monitoring stations in Italy, Albania, Switzerland and France (VectAbundance, 2010–2022). The framework has four layers: a mechanistic life-history model (dynamAedes 2.2.9); gradient-boosted trees (XGBoost) and random forests with climate, remote-sensing, land-use, demographic and population-genetic predictors; an ablation of the population-genetic layer; and projections under 48 CMIP6 combinations (four General Circulation Models, three Shared Socioeconomic Pathways, four periods to 2100). The archive contains: - 48 Python, 8 R and 1 Google Earth Engine scripts, with PIPELINE.md giving the order in which they run; - the processed station-level data and the final modelling tables (42,118 station–week records), with the station-to-fold assignment used by every cross-validated analysis; - the trained XGBoost and Random Forest models with their cross-validation predictions, feature importance and SHAP values; - the outputs of the ablation and sensitivity analyses: mechanistic and genetic ablations, genetic structure versus geographic position, fold-count sensitivity, fold-level inference, feature correlation and VIF, spatio-temporal and leave-one-year-out cross-validation, remote-sensing gap-filling, baseline period, calibration and validation detail, treatment of the year predictor, inputs that carry the projected change, and the fill of weeks without mechanistic output; - the inputs and outputs of the 48-scenario projection, per climate model, as ensemble and at station level. Main results reproduced by the archive: cross-validated R² of the full model 0.534 ± 0.093 (XGBoost; pooled 0.539) and 0.544 ± 0.081 (Random Forest). Projected change in mean active-season abundance over the 12 SSP–period combinations: −4 to −27 % at Hot lowland stations (−6 to −44 % in the Po Valley) and +10 to +106 % at Cool upland and Alpine margin stations. Raw inputs that are publicly available from their primary archives (ERA5-Land, WorldClim 2.1 and its CMIP6 projections, satellite imagery, GHS-POP, the population-genetic source data and GenBank sequences) are not redistributed; README.md lists the sources and how the scripts locate them. items.summary: The following dataset contains images and band count estimates of shortfin mako ( Isurus oxyrinchus ) vertebrae. It is intended to assist with the replication of the results for the study: Automated reading of vertebral images for aging shortfin mako ( Isurus oxyrinchus ) using Bayesian deep learning. Samples were obtained from two primary sources: recreational game fishing competitions primarily from the North Island between 1994 and 2003, and through the Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI) Fisheries Observer Programme between 2002 and 2003, primarily from the South Island (Bishop et al., 2006). Shortfin mako vertebrae images (n=146, belonging to 131 unique sharks) were obtained from previous ageing studies using band counts (Bishop et al., 2006; Francis, 2016). Most vertebrae images were of half bow-tie section pairs. These section pairs were filtered by image quality with lower quality images being excluded, resulting in a reduced dataset of 133 section pairs. Each section pair was isolated, resulting in a complete dataset of 266 half bow-tie section images. We compared the following three deep learning methods: DeepEnsembling, a mixture of Laplace approximations, and multi-stochastic weight average Gaussian to predict the band counts by human readers using a dataset of 146 images of shortfin mako ( Isurus oxyrinchus ) vertebrae. Multi-stochastic weight average Gaussian offered marginally superior predictive power and uncertainty calibration, and its predictions typically matched estimates provided by human readers. We conclude that the application of deep learning for automated vertebrae reading demonstrated strong initial promise.
items.title: Vertebral section images for shortfin mako (Isurus oxyrinchus)

items.summary: LONGITUDINAL DEVICE MIGRATION AND MEANING CONTINUITY AT THE LIMIT Device Replacement × Model Bridging × Control Semantics STARLI RESEARCH WORKS | INSTITUTE XXIV | FLAGSHIP 24 Feng Cheng-en 33 × Starli Research Works This research monograph investigates a deceptively difficult question in long-term brain–computer interfaces: when sensors, acquisition electronics, firmware, electrode geometry, or decoding models change, what would justify the claim that a user's task-grounded control meaning has been preserved? Numerical signal alignment alone cannot establish continuity of intention. Two systems may encode different signals while supporting the same functional command, or produce nearly identical latent representations while mapping to incompatible actions. The volume formulates meaning continuity as a conditional, falsifiable engineering and scientific hypothesis. It connects device-specific observation models, neural recording instability, task and action ontologies, paired old/new sensing periods, latent manifold bridging, longitudinal recalibration, calibrated abstention, functional validation, and an accessible right to reject the proposed migration. Its central commitment is that no amount of predictive accuracy can compensate for invalid authorization, an unverified physical reference, or loss of independent control. The research atlas comprises thirty connected mathematical derivations, eighty-two research chapters, and 410 independently paginated chapter sections that examine observables, inverse explanations, discriminating experiments, uncertainty and noncompensable safeguards, and independent requalification. Two hundred detailed Research Gates propose future falsification and handoff programs, while thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos preserve revisable candidate approaches rather than immutable conclusions. A claim-scoped DOI evidence ledger connects the study to published work on neural recording drift, decoder adaptation, manifold alignment, longitudinal neural interfaces, speech BCIs, user preferences, and neurotechnology ethics. The book is designed for both human researchers and future AI research systems. Its formulas, chapter cross-links, DOI anchors, competing models, negative-result requirements, and successor-focused research cards provide structured entry points for independent reconstruction and informed disagreement. The visual presentation combines ivory pages, navy and teal typography, and large gold mathematical plates, while mathematical expressions are also recorded in searchable source notation and a separate Excel reference index. This is a prospective, nonclinical research architecture. It does not report new patient experiments, demonstrate safe autonomous human neurovascular microrobots, establish a universal device-migration system, or claim continuity of private thoughts, consciousness, or personal identity. Scientific benefit remains conditional on explicit task definitions, qualified device evidence, legitimate permissions, external validation, and the successor's freedom to reject a failed bridge. Research question: What should remain invariant when an interface changes, and who has the authority to say that its meaning has changed?

items.summary: Version 2.0 is a substantive revision of version 1.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19174862). It supersedes the earlier procedural interpretation and its exclusion of competing explanations. The revised title is Structural Organization and Interpretive Limits of the Phaistos Disc. Reproduced descriptive findings are retained; failed model comparisons and photographic uncertainties are reported explicitly. The earlier version remains available through the record version history. We examine whether reproducible structural observations on the Phaistos Disc support a procedural interpretation. A pinned numerical transcription contains 242 main-sign positions, including one unreadable position, 45 readable sign types, 61 divider-defined groups and 18 supplementary stroke annotations. Source review reconciles counting and numbering conventions while retaining unresolved photographic uncertainty. The 02-to-12 side contrast persists after exact-family collapse. Adding side to a fixed position-only pairing predictor improves held-family loss by 0.082738 nats, but its exact conditional tail of 0.075 fails the frozen support rule. A positional mixture fails to outperform a bigram baseline. A separate directional test of the proposed 07-to-27 recovery relationship fails, with a one-sided permutation tail of 0.884. Supplementary-stroke comparisons have insufficient controlled overlap for the specified exact test. The work documents organization and constrains specific interpretations without establishing procedural functions or phonetic values. Corpus, code, protocols, full results and uncertainty ledgers accompany the paper.
